:::{#cor-log-below-tangent}
#### The natural logarithm lies below its tangent line at one

For every $t > 0$,

$$\logf{t} \le t - 1,$$

with equality exactly when $t = 1$.

:::

::: proof

Put $x = \logf{t}$,
so that $\expf{x} = t$ by the [inverse relation of the logarithm and the exponential](algebra.qmd#thm-exp-log-inverse).
By @thm-exp-above-tangent, $t = \expf{x} \ge 1 + x = 1 + \logf{t}$,
which is $\logf{t} \le t - 1$.
Equality holds exactly when $x = 0$,
that is, when $\logf{t} = 0$,
that is, when $t = 1$.

:::
